The affine margin average is the margin at Y. If Y belongs to the closed cap, at least one tuple occurrence has nonnegative margin, including when all margins are zero. A profile that is nonnegative and one there therefore pays one per tuple.

At distinct uniform physical fibers, original captured mass is the volume-weighted sum of captured probabilities and is at least the smallest original volume times their sum. Arbitrary base tilts are retained by the lifted affine identity.

Nonnegative incidence costs count repeated occurrences, so integrating against feasible tuple weights charges every physical atom at most its budget. The finite primal is bounded by total input mass, and finite LP duality gives the nonnegative cover and attainment. Empty tuple families give zero.

For the continuous lower-bound extension, summing the exact cap inequalities against the tuple measures and applying marginal domination controls the same original cap. There is no use of atomic approximations preserving an equality constraint.

The linked revision explicitly limits the LP to finitely supported atomic sources. Finitely many types and finitely many atoms give finitely many tuples, so the nonempty bounded closed primal polytope and finite duality apply as claimed. The continuous assertion retains only the integrated cap quota.

The continuous statement only supplies the cap lower bound and does not prove that countable dual.
